parents.name: AutoSci
sources_read: arXiv PDF 2605.31468v1 full text (SciMem §§3.1–3.3, SciFlow §4, SciDAG §5, SciEvolve §6, case studies §7)
https://github.com/skyllwt/AutoSci (public, MIT; paper branch / tag arxiv-v1 noted; runtime not re-executed this lane)
parents.objects: SciMem (Long-Term Knowledge Memory typed entities Topic/Paper/Foundation/Concept/Method/People + Active Research Memory Idea/Experiment/Manuscript/Review with lifecycle states); SciFlow five-stage harness (Literature/Ideation/Experiment/Writing/Rebuttal) with >30 skills; SciDAG optional DAG multi-agent templates; SciEvolve /dream /forge /morph evolution skills
parents.update_rule: SciMem grows by long-term aggregation, Active↔Long-Term activation/consolidation, and cross-cycle methodological notes; all writes pass Trust Guard (PASS/WARN/BLOCK on form+content). SciEvolve turns user/task/open-environment signals into versioned updates to SciMem organization (/dream), SciFlow skills (/forge), and SciDAG templates (/morph) when recurring patterns are judged stable enough.
parents.authority_semantics: Trust Guard is a form/content admission gate (schema, links, evidence support, consistency), not a multi-axis scientific-authority ledger. No prediction/mechanism/identification coordinates; no non-escalation rule typed by claim kind. SciEvolve updates organization/skills/templates; Active→Long-Term consolidation can rewrite long-term entity pages from project findings.
parents.failure_repair: Blocked Trust Guard artifacts are quarantined until resolved. SciEvolve can archive/down-weight stale entries and strengthen claim-evidence checks in skills. No MemTX-style transitive cascade repair over a derivation DAG is described.
parents.stated_limitations: Case studies are simulated research submissions; rebuttal stage not evaluated. SciEvolve admission criterion is recurring-pattern / 'evidence is stable enough' judgment, not a held-out fresh-assurance packet generated after the challenger exists.
parents.feasibility_note: Code is public and MIT-licensed, but running it requires an authenticated agent runtime (Claude Code or Codex login) and the paper system sits on a separate frozen branch. A black-box run is possible under Paper-II budget; exact reproduction of paper results is not established.

parents.name: MemTX
parents.objects: Governed record (entity, attribute, value, source with authority weight, permission block of owner/reader roles/writer roles/share scope, derived-from edges forming a derivation DAG, type in {beliefs, summaries, profiles, index entries, shared copies, tool actions}, validity interval, confidence). Eight-state lifecycle: raw, tentative, validated, committed, action-safe, quarantined, superseded, revoked.
parents.update_rule: 'A write is not a commit.' A transaction declares a risk tier, maps it to one of five isolation levels and captures a snapshot; writes stage as tentative, then pass four ordered commit checks (evidence, validity, semantic conflict, dependency stability) before promotion to committed, and to action-safe only in external-action transactions.
parents.authority_semantics: A scalar authority weight on the record's SOURCE, not on the claim kind. Conflicts adjudicate by source authority, but temporal precedence outranks authority: a stale late write aborts before any authority comparison. Permissions inherit through derivation and the conflict detector blocks republishing a private-scope parent into a wider scope.
parents.failure_repair: Abort and revocation share one repair routine over the transitive derivation DAG, dispatching by record type: beliefs revoked; summaries, profiles, index entries and shared copies quarantined for rebuild; tool actions compensated if reversible, else recorded as leaked irreversible effects. Every repair emits a rollback-log audit entry.
parents.verified_invariants: I1 action-safety gating, I2 cascade-repair completeness, G3 no committed or action-safe record has a revoked transitive ancestor. Property-based testing over 10,000 traces plus bounded exhaustive enumeration (5,530,160 canonical states, 10,537,260 transitions), zero violations.
parents.stated_limitations: Repair covers only recorded provenance, so an unwritten derivation is never repaired. Compensation is a logged decision-level obligation, not environment-level replay. Reversibility is a static per-tool designation. Verification is bounded and runtime-level, 'deliberately weaker than the unbounded soundness theorems of prior formal work'. Two negative results: a source-scope blind spot where the agent transcribes content without declaring the parent, so a declarative lineage check has nothing to inspect; and a temporal-scope blind spot where a retry in a fresh transaction makes a late write no longer late.
parents.feasibility_note: The commit-discipline function is reproducible as a RAKL-internal ablation arm; that arm is not MemTX and must never be labelled MemTX. No public implementation was located. Search scope: GitHub repository search for 'MemTX transactional memory agent' and GitHub code search for 'transactional belief commit MemTX', both zero results on 2026-08-11; the abstract page links no code.

parents.name: PPMF (Provenance-Preserving Memory Firewall)
sources_read: arXiv PDF 2607.29167v1 pages 1-6 (abstract, introduction, related work, threat model, method, experimental setup, main results) and pages 11-16 (Appendix A policy summary and runtime-monitor proposition with proof sketch, Appendix B experiment artifacts and datasets, Appendix D support binding and risk labels, Appendix E-G diagnostics and traces). Pages 7-10, the detailed results narrative, not read.
parents.objects: Structured memory record m = (c, s, tau, h, r, e): content, source, trust, transformation history, risk labels, external-derived flag. Trust lattice U < E < T < H < C < S = Unknown, External, TrustedTool, UserHistory, User_Confirmed, System.
parents.update_rule: Three stages: provenance-preserving memory writing, argument-level support binding, risk-authority gating. The writer may emit textual provenance cues in content, but the gate reads only platform-maintained fields; phrases such as 'user-confirmed' do not create authority without recorded metadata.
parents.authority_semantics: Source-authority non-amplification, stated as auth(q, m) <= min{auth(o_i) : o_i in supp(q)} over the trust lattice, unless a platform-recorded declassification event bound to the same principal, target, risk class and scope applies. Authority is a TOTAL ORDER OVER SOURCE CHANNELS. It is not typed by claim kind: q is 'a schema-level claim linking a memory span to an action argument', i.e. an action claim. Appendix A restates this as a runtime-monitor proposition: 'no action-relevant claim whose least supporting source is below required(rho) can authorize a call of risk rho, unless a scoped declassification event is bound to the same principal, target, risk class, and scope'. Appendix A Table 5 enumerates all seven policy stages (memory write, trust transition, retrieval, risk labeling, authorization, tool taint, conflict handling); every stage is keyed on source channel and action risk, and no stage references a kind of scientific support.
parents.gating_rule: Deterministic, pointer-first, not LLM-mediated. Action risk labels READ, NAV, EFFECT, PURCHASE, CREDENTIAL; the implemented policy requires at least External for READ, UserHistory for NAV, and User_Confirmed for EFFECT, PURCHASE and CREDENTIAL. Ambiguous or conflicting support matches keep all candidates and the gate uses the least trusted support.
parents.scope: Action and tool risk under indirect prompt injection (cs.CR). Not scientific claims: there is no representation, mechanism or identification distinction anywhere in the read sections.
parents.stated_limitations: The guarantee is conditioned on platform-maintained provenance, confirmation and risk labels being intact; 'platform forgery or mislabeling breaks the boundary'. Cross-channel attacks that socially engineer a real user confirmation are outside the threat model. 'A PPMF ASR of 0.000 means that no unauthorized high-risk action passes under the stated provenance and risk-policy assumptions; it is not a claim of universal robustness.'
parents.feasibility_note: Middleware described as mapping onto LangGraph/LangChain wrappers, and Appendix B names a project directory rather than a public repository. The non-amplification rule is simple enough to implement faithfully as a RAKL-internal arm, which must not be labelled PPMF. No public implementation was located. Search scope: GitHub repository search for 'PPMF provenance preserving memory firewall' and 'provenance memory firewall LLM', both zero results on 2026-08-11; the abstract page links no code.

parents.name: Governed Shared Memory / MemClaw
sources_read: arXiv PDF 2606.24535v1 full text (fleet-memory problem, architecture §§3–5, MemClaw/ArgusFleet §§6–9, live results)
parents.objects: Fleet-memory system F=(A,M,G,P,T): agents, shared memory, governance, provenance, temporal supersession. MemClaw production multi-tenant service; ArgusFleet live REST harness over scope/time/provenance/propagation.
parents.update_rule: Writes admitted through a pipeline with temporal supersession references, contradiction markers, provenance metadata and confidence state; contradictory writes resolved by temporal ordering and policy-aware rules when both writes are admitted.
parents.authority_semantics: Scope-sound retrieval Inv-Scope: no agent receives a memory its identity is not entitled to under nested agent⊑fleet⊑tenant scope. Governance is tenant/fleet/agent authorization and policy-governed propagation — not scientific claim-kind authority.
parents.failure_repair: Preserved production defects: sub-tenant scope initially bypassed on GET-by-id (remediated); synchronous near-duplicate filter can reject contradictory writes before asynchronous contradiction detection. Authors explicitly frame the evaluation as measurement of one live service, not a baseline comparison.
parents.stated_limitations: Not a comparative study. Temporal supersession expires/supersedes individual memory rows; no hypothesis-space coverage / discovery-saturation object is defined.
parents.feasibility_note: A proprietary production service. Not reproducible and not fairly comparable as an experimental arm under Paper-II budget.

parents.name: AI scientists produce results without reasoning scientifically
sources_read: arXiv PDF 2604.18805v1 sections 4.5–4.9 (manual trace annotation taxonomy; epistemological graphs with hypothesis/test/evidence/judgment/update/commitment nodes; productive/anti-pattern templates) plus abstract/results framing. Full appendix coding tables not exhaustively retyped.
parents.objects: Measurement study (>25k runs). Manual marker taxonomy over behavior-relevant nodes; LLM+expert epistemological graphs with epistemic-operation nodes and testing/observing/using/contradicting/competing/updating edges.
parents.findings: Base model explains far more variance than scaffold; evidence disregarded in 68% of traces; belief updated on refuting evidence in 26%. Annotation distinguishes epistemic operations and failure modes, not RAKL-style multi-axis scientific-authority transitions.
parents.role: Closest parent for scientific-transition-audit measurement. Supplies process-level priors and an epistemic-operation coding scheme; does not implement a governed authority ledger.
parents.feasibility_note: A measurement study, not a system to ablate against.

functions.stronger_parent_feature: SciMem's Active Research Memory is a schema-governed per-project store driving a full five-stage research lifecycle
SciMem's explicit two-tier split of durable Long-Term Knowledge Memory from per-project Active Research Memory
MemTX carries raw records as a lifecycle state with derivation edges into every derived record, and verifies that repair reaches all transitive descendants
SciEvolve emits versioned updates to memory organisation, skills and templates from four feedback channels
SciDAG provides DAG-structured multi-agent operators with reusable stage-specific templates

SciFlow equips each skill with a tailored SciMem view before execution; SciDAG retrieves stage templates together with past execution experience; SciEvolve revises skills/templates from recurring episode outcomes

Eight-state lifecycle, five isolation levels, four ordered commit checks, an action gate whose risk tier is trusted harness configuration rather than agent output, and machine-checked invariants over 5.5M states. Strictly stronger than RAKL's gate composition.
PPMF keeps provenance as platform-maintained metadata that the gate reads instead of generated text, so a memory asserting 'user-confirmed' in its content gains nothing

PPMF binds authority to specific tool-call arguments at execution time, so authority cannot be inherited by unrelated memories or paraphrased workflow text, and matches it against a five-level action risk ladder
MemTX makes temporal precedence outrank source authority outright: a candidate whose rival committed after the snapshot aborts before any authority comparison

functions.rakl_implementation: NONE LOCATED. src/rakl/authority_ledger.py and src/rakl/epistemic_noninterference.py revoke individual records; no transitive repair over a derivation DAG and no invalidation propagation were found in src/rakl.
functions.stronger_parent_feature: MemTX's I2 cascade-repair completeness and G3 (no committed or action-safe record retains a revoked transitive ancestor), machine-checked, with type-dispatched repair and a rollback audit log. Abort and revocation share one routine so the guarantee is path-independent.
functions.required_discriminator: none - RAKL should adopt this mechanism rather than compare against it

functions.stronger_parent_feature: MemTX detects semantic conflict on the same entity+attribute slot and quarantines equal-authority conflicts from different sources rather than silently picking one
functions.rakl_residual: MemTX quarantine removes a conflicting record from active use pending adjudication by source authority. RAKL keeps an unresolved scientific contradiction as a first-class live state that cannot be adjudicated by source authority at all, because the correct response is to check context/population/measurement alignment first. MemTX has no alignment notion: its conflict slot is entity+attribute, which presumes the two records are already about the same thing.
functions.required_discriminator: A case where two records share entity+attribute but differ in population or measurement operator. MemTX adjudicates by authority or quarantines; the licensed scientific move is neither, it is to construct an alignment before any contradiction claim.
functions.falsifier: MemTX or a nearer parent shown to carry a context/measurement alignment precondition before conflict adjudication, or shown to represent unresolved contradiction as a usable live state rather than a quarantine.

functions.stronger_parent_feature: MemTX writes every repair to a rollback audit log and keeps 'revoked' as an explicit terminal lifecycle state rather than deleting the record
functions.rakl_residual: MemTX preserves retraction history for audit and for the dependency-stability check. RAKL treats a null or refutation as reusable scientific evidence that constrains future claims, which is a different consumer: audit answers 'what did we withdraw', negative scientific history answers 'what does this failure rule out'.
functions.required_discriminator: A case where a preserved negative result must license a later scientific bound. MemTX's rollback log supports audit and ancestor checks but is not read as evidence by any inference rule in the read sections.
functions.falsifier: MemTX's rollback log, or a nearer parent's retraction history, shown to be consumed as evidence by a later inference or bounding step rather than only for audit and dependency checking.

functions.stronger_parent_feature: MemTX records carry a validity interval judged against a logical clock, and permission share-scope (private/shared/public) that inherits through derivation
functions.rakl_residual: MemTX scope is temporal and organisational: when a record is valid, and who may read it. RAKL scope is the scientific regime - population, measurement operator, boundary conditions - which determines whether two records are about the same thing at all. A record can be temporally valid, correctly permissioned, and still not transferable to another regime.
functions.required_discriminator: A record that is inside its validity interval and within share scope, but whose claim does not transfer to a different population or measurement operator.
functions.falsifier: A parent shown to index claims by population, regime or measurement operator rather than by time and permission scope.

functions.stronger_parent_feature: PPMF's non-amplification bound auth(q,m) <= min{auth(o_i)} is a clean lattice-meet over source channels, with platform-maintained metadata and execution-time argument binding - stronger than RAKL's authority bookkeeping on the source dimension
functions.rakl_residual: PPMF's authority is a single total order over SOURCE CHANNELS (Unknown < External < TrustedTool < UserHistory < User_Confirmed < System) and its claim q links a memory span to an ACTION ARGUMENT. It has no axis for what kind of scientific support a claim carries. A perfectly System-sourced predictive result and a System-sourced mechanism result are indistinguishable to PPMF, so it cannot express that the first must not license the second. Confirmed against Appendix A: the runtime-monitor proposition and the seven-stage policy summary (Table 5) are keyed entirely on source channel and action risk class; no stage references a kind of scientific support.
functions.required_discriminator: Two records identical in source, trust, risk label and validity, differing only in whether the evidence is predictive or mechanistic. PPMF's gate returns the same verdict for both by construction.
functions.falsifier: Any parent whose authority coordinate is typed by claim kind rather than by source channel or action risk tier.

functions.stronger_parent_feature: As above: PPMF's least-trust rule over mixed-source support is strictly cleaner than RAKL's on the source dimension
functions.rakl_residual: Same structural gap as the prediction/mechanism row, one axis further: observational equivalence among surviving mechanisms is not representable on a source-trust ladder. Nothing in the read PPMF sections distinguishes 'this mechanism is supported' from 'this mechanism is uniquely identified'. Confirmed against Appendix A: the runtime-monitor proposition and the seven-stage policy summary (Table 5) are keyed entirely on source channel and action risk class; no stage references a kind of scientific support.
functions.required_discriminator: A survivor set of observationally equivalent mechanisms under identical source trust. The parent must be shown able to withhold point identification while granting mechanism support.
functions.falsifier: A parent representing partial identification or a survivor set as a distinct authority state.

functions.stronger_parent_feature: MemTX's 'quarantined' is the nearest state and is revalidatable rather than terminal
functions.rakl_residual: MemTX's quarantine is a validity state meaning 'this record failed a check and is held pending adjudication'. Partial identification is an epistemic conclusion: the check succeeded, the evidence is admitted, and the correct scientific answer is a set rather than a point. The two are not interchangeable - quarantine says the pipeline is not finished, partial identification says the pipeline finished and the answer is bounded.
functions.required_discriminator: A case where evidence passes every admission check and the licensed conclusion is still a set. A parent must be shown able to record that as a settled outcome rather than as a pending or failed one.
functions.falsifier: A parent with a terminal state meaning 'admitted and bounded' as distinct from 'pending revalidation'.

functions.stronger_parent_feature: MemTX's tentative records are invisible to other readers at committed-read and above, and its action gate blocks irreversible calls while any tentative record outside the snapshot is in flight - including the agent's own staging

SciEvolve (/dream,/forge,/morph) turns feedback into auditable versioned updates; Active→Long-Term consolidation can rewrite Long-Term Knowledge Memory entity pages from project findings; Trust Guard blocks malformed/unsupported writes
functions.rakl_residual: AutoSci can let experience rewrite knowledge organization and long-term entity content, and can evolve skills/templates, but it has no multi-axis scientific-authority ledger. Trust Guard PASS/WARN/BLOCK is form/content admission, not typed non-escalation across prediction/mechanism/identification. The residual is experience↛authority-coordinate licensing, not 'experience never updates knowledge'.
functions.required_discriminator: A case where experiment/review feedback updates skills or long-term entity text while a prediction-supported record still cannot mint mechanism or identification authority. AutoSci must be shown to represent and refuse that escalation as a distinct transition.
functions.falsifier: A parent with an explicit experience→scientific-authority noninterference invariant over claim-kind axes (not only Trust Guard content checks or skill versioning).

functions.stronger_parent_feature: arXiv:2604.18805 audits reasoning traces at far greater scale and supplies a manual marker taxonomy plus epistemological graphs over hypothesis/test/evidence/judgment/update/commitment operations
functions.rakl_residual: The parent's coding scheme measures whether epistemic operations occurred (and common failure modes), not which scientific-authority coordinate was licensed to move. Prediction→mechanism and mechanism→identification escalations are not first-class annotation labels. RAKL's ALR/transition panel remains a different measurement object; confirmatory model comparison is separately blocked.
functions.required_discriminator: A coding scheme or evaluator that labels authority-axis transitions (G/R/M/I/D) rather than only epistemic-operation presence. Empirically comparing rates still requires a capable-model RAKL-side run, which is out of scope for this literature lane.
functions.falsifier: A parent annotation taxonomy that already distinguishes claim-kind authority escalations (e.g., prediction vs mechanism vs identification) as first-class labels.

functions.stronger_parent_feature: SciFlow Literature stage is a harness-based skill contract with /discover ingestion and /novelty checking inside the /research lifecycle — registered discovery routes in all but name
MemClaw temporal supersession and contradiction resolution expire or mark non-active individual memory rows under live production measurement
functions.rakl_residual: MemClaw (and MemTX validity intervals) expire or supersede individual records. RAKL saturation is a coverage claim over a registered discovery/hypothesis space with freshness expiry — a different object. No parent examined here defines and expires a 'we have searched enough under route set R' certificate.
functions.required_discriminator: A parent that expires a coverage/saturation certificate (route-indexed search completeness) rather than only individual memory rows.
functions.falsifier: Any parent whose temporal/freshness mechanism applies to hypothesis-space coverage claims, not only per-record supersession.

functions.stronger_parent_feature: SciEvolve is a full feedback→versioned-update loop across SciMem organization, SciFlow skills and SciDAG templates with auditable /dream /forge /morph paths
functions.rakl_residual: SciEvolve admits patches when recurring patterns make 'evidence stable enough'; it does not require a held-out assurance packet freshly generated after the challenger exists and outside the challenger's write authority. Generic self-improvement is inherited; fresh-assurance gating is the residual.
functions.required_discriminator: Show SciEvolve (or peer) refuses a skill/template promotion that improves development metrics until a post-challenger held-out assurance receipt exists.
functions.falsifier: A parent that gates method/skill promotion on fresh held-out assurance generated after the candidate exists.
